message.content:
First reduce the bases modulo \(11\):

\[
129 \div 11 \text{ leaves remainder } 8
\]
\[
96 \div 11 \text{ leaves remainder } 8
\]

So,

\[
129^{34}+96^{38} \equiv 8^{34}+8^{38} \pmod{11}
\]

Since \(8\) and \(11\) are coprime, we can use Fermat’s theorem: \(8^{10}\equiv 1 \pmod{11}\).

Reduce the exponents modulo \(10\):

\[
34 \equiv 4 \pmod{10}, \qquad 38 \equiv 8 \pmod{10}
\]

Thus,

\[
8^{34}+8^{38} \equiv 8^4+8^8 \pmod{11}
\]

Now compute powers:

\[
8^2 = 64 \equiv 9 \pmod{11}
\]

\[
8^4 = (8^2)^2 \equiv 9^2 = 81 \equiv 4 \pmod{11}
\]

\[
8^8 = (8^4)^2 \equiv 4^2 = 16 \equiv 5 \pmod{11}
\]

So,

\[
8^4+8^8 \equiv 4+5=9 \pmod{11}
\]

The answer is 9.
